text:
alex_k: Hey team — big customer (AcmeHealth) reporting p99 latency jumps on API calls that use tool/function calling + structured JSON outputs. They saw p95 go from ~120ms -> ~420ms and p99 up to ~1.2s starting ~2026-03-14 22:30 UTC. They’re seeing timeouts and billing complaints. Can we triage?

maria_support: escalating. Customer sent sample request and response sizes. Request includes tool_router route to `doc_search` and `code_exec`, structured output schema for `analysis` ~ 2.6 KB.

samir_sre: I pulled metrics — spike aligns with increased fraction of requests hitting the tool router path. Queue length on runtime goroutines for tool routing increased ~3x. Quick numbers: tool-routing latency p95 from 40ms -> 230ms, schema-validation CPU from 5ms -> 180ms per request on some hosts.

jordan_runtime: logs show schema-validator process (python lib) running in-process before streaming start. Stack: request handler -> tool-router -> schema-validate -> streaming. That blocks sending tokens until validation completes. Example snippet from host logs:```[2076543239] INFO tool-router: matched route=code_exec id=doc_search latency_ms=215
[2076543240] WARN schema-validator: validation_time_ms=178 size_bytes=2600
[2076543241] DEBUG stream: waiting_for_validation```\n
lee_ml: we recently merged PR that enforces full JSON schema validation for structured outputs (strict mode) and also added an expensive regex check for field formats. Could be the regression. PR merged 2026-03-14 20:10 UTC — timing lines up.

alex_k: customer wants quick mitigation — they can’t tolerate 1.2s p99. What short-term toggles do we have?

samir_sre: short-term mitigation options: 1) flip schema validation to `fast` mode (shallow types only) via runtime feature flag; 2) route heavy tool calls to dedicated pool (lower CPU contention); 3) enable upstream streaming-before-validation to let tokens flow while validation runs async — but risky for strict output correctness.

jordan_runtime: implemented a runtime feature flag `structured_validation_mode` (values: strict, fast, disabled). We can toggle to `fast` for AcmeHealth account only. I can push a canary for that account to take effect in ~4 minutes. Also we can switch tool-router policy to prefer dedicated nodes for these routes; that needs a config change but low risk.

maria_support: Please do both — customer agreed to `fast` validation + dedicated routing while we root cause. They asked for repro steps we can share.

samir_sre: repro steps I used: 1) Use sample request payload (attached) with tool calls to `doc_search` + structured output schema; 2) run 1000 concurrent requests with seq_len ~512 and measure tool-router and validation times; 3) observe host CPU and disk io. I captured flamegraph pointing at `jsonschema.validate` and some expensive `re.compile` calls.

lee_ml: follow-up: I’ll open quick PR to memoize compiled regex and precompile schemas per model-version to avoid repeated compile cost. That should drop validation_time_ms from ~180ms -> ~6-10ms in worst cases. Longer term we want streaming-validated mode where we incrementally validate; that’s a few sprints out.

jordan_runtime: canary toggle done for AcmeHealth at 2076543265 — switched `structured_validation_mode` -> `fast` and updated routing policy to prefer `dedicated-tool-pool`. Observability: within one minute p95 dropped back to ~150ms, p99 ~320ms. Still higher than baseline but acceptable to customer for now.

maria_support: reported back to customer and asked them to validate. They responded: "looks better, no timeouts so far; still slightly slower but acceptable for now. please keep us posted." :thumbsup:

samir_sre: next actions: - lee: PR to memoize regex & precompile schema (high). - jordan: instrument schema-validate timing per-request + expose metric `schema_validation_time_ms` to Console per-route. - ops: consider autoscale policy for `dedicated-tool-pool` to handle backfills. - support: keep AcmeHealth on canary until regression fully mitigated.

alex_k: adding follow-ups to ticket. Also filing incident note for postmortem — root cause = strict regex + in-process validation blocking streaming, exacerbated by routing shift (more requests hitting tool path).

ops-bot: deploy pipeline notification: `feature/fast-schema-toggle` applied to canary (acmehealth) at 2076543266 by jordan_runtime.

maria_support: thanks all. keeping thread open until lee confirms PR and we have permanent rollout plan.

lee_ml: PR opened 2076543305 -> MR link: https://git.redwood/lee/memoize-schema (will request review). I’ll also add unit test for precompiled regex. ETA to prod patch ~48h.

samir_sre: timeline wise, if PR merges and we release tomorrow, we can revert canary and safely go back to `strict` (or keep `fast` as default if strict unnecessary). I’ll prepare SLO spike dashboard and add an alert for schema_validation_time_ms > 50ms for >5m.

alex_k: great. capturing all on the customer ticket. thanks team.
